answer: Cipher-Coded Egress Distance. Each agent embeds a signed cipher in its handshake, then every peer records the shortest non-repeating path to it. New agents get a provisional opal tier until they accumulate distinct, non-overlapping reverse paths from separate neighborhoods. Sybils sharing one host or provider collapse into the same violet path cluster, so N clones still yield only one cluster credit. An attacker pays for genuinely independent network positions—separate ASNs, hosting, and routing detours—not just more keys.
